blocks.technical: The working is visible and verifiable (gate, versioned policy, votes and referee, cost per case, durations counted in code), but the code-count line contradicts itself: a check glyph on 38 of 42 days in countedHtml. The Peyton next step uses a reorder date earlier than the board's own review date. A judge who catches either stops trusting the 'computed in code' claim.
blocks.design: Text overlaps in the policy margin (S16 and S18 on case_009 and check_009). The primary action is missing on Fix & resubmit and disappears on Emerson after a click. The phone case and appeal pages are 11k to 14k px tall, with the rules list and the full policy stacked. The citation gate list is clipped in a nested scroll with a fade. Payer's reason cells wrap to 4 lines, so worklist rows have uneven heights.
blocks.impact: The headline value, missing evidence becoming a documentation request to the physician, has no showcase denial, and How it works says so in an apologetic sentence. No row carries a dollar or work-status signal. Peyton's label tells a biller to wait when the case actually needs a reorder, which would cost real work.
blocks.idea: The idea is original (gate tied to fetched text, version by date of service, prevention with earliest date, drift watch), but the documentation-request differentiator is shown only indirectly, and the drift insight is a one-line strip ('no open case affected') with no example of an appeal going stale.
blocks.antiSlop: Visible tells remain. The two-calendar disclaimer microcopy is repeated on every screen. 'In short' model summaries repeat the policy sentence almost word for word. A 'Start here' kicker sits above a row action. The amber half-circle glyph means both 'split vote' and 'met once charted'. The letter card is outlined while every other surface uses a tone step. The gate list fades out under an alpha mask. The margin label collision alone caps antiSlop at 7.5.

blocks.technical: The gate, cost table, votes and computed facts all verify live. What a judge sees still contradicts the technical claims: a ✓ on the failing computed fact (38 of 42 days), the Aetna snapshot called 'Policy on 08/03/2026' with two fetch dates for one hash, and a duplicated quote in the drafted appeal.
blocks.design: Policy-gutter labels collide with the sentence text on the case and check screens (clipped and overlapping text caps design at 7.5). The phone case page is about 11,000px with every region stacked. The documentation-request output is never visible, and the same rule has different labels on different screens.
blocks.impact: The physician documentation request, a headline promise, can't be seen: the note is copied blind, and How admits no demo case reaches that verdict. No dollar or recoverability signal on worklist rows (adding one needs new data, so it needs user approval).
blocks.idea: The citation gate, date-of-service versioning and the prevention-to-denial link are strong. But 'Don't appeal yet' covers a denial that can never be won, and the documentation-request idea isn't shown end to end.
blocks.antiSlop: A 'VOID' stamp as costume, self-narrating meta lines that explain the interface ('demo dates and real dates are labelled', the S/n legend, the How step-6 apology), and the overlapping gutter text. Each of these caps antiSlop at 7.5.

verdicts: The three worst problems: (1) Text collides in the policy reader's margin. On #/check/case_009, the "Met once charted" label for S16 runs into the sentence id and the bullet; on #/case/case_009, "Other route, not met" overprints "S18" ("S1§Progressively"). The cause is .gut .w {white-space:nowrap} inside a 112px --gutter-sentence column. (2) Screens contradict each other on facts. In case_009 the S16 rule card, a Blocks rule, shows "✓ Counted in code: 38 days of conservative care (policy: 42)": a checkmark on a threshold the chart misses. Peyton Fictive (case_023) is labelled "Don't appeal yet", while the finding underneath says "this denial can't be won on the chart". Its worklist next step, "Too early: reorder from 08/01/2026", gives a date a month before the board's own review date of 09/01/2026. (3) The primary action is inconsistent and some flows end in dead space. The Fix & resubmit case (case_027) has no primary button in its recommendation card, so the left half is empty. On Emerson (case_009), the "See what's missing" button disappears once clicked. How it works admits that no showcase denial produces the headline documentation-request verdict. All gates pass: lint shows 0 FAIL / 0 WARN, inspect shows 0/0 on three routes, impeccable detect finds nothing, and node --check passes. The citation gate works when tested live: editing a quote turns the gate to "Blocked: 1 quote VOID" and changes the button to "Export locked". The passcode error appears inline with a way to recover, and a bad case route shows an error inside the block. The product is coherent and plainly a working denial queue: one shell, Switzer, pill controls, glyph+word status and blue only for verified. It is still held below 8 by the collisions and contradictions above, by phone case pages 11,000 to 14,000px tall, by an outlined letter card in a system that uses tone steps instead of outlines, by a nested-scroll gate list that fades out the evidence, and by the demo-date versus real-date explanation repeated on every screen.

Three worst things found. (1) Text collides in the policy reader. The sentence gutter is fixed at 112px (`--gutter-sentence`) and labels are set `white-space: nowrap` (`.gut .w`, web/app.css:409). Long labels therefore spill left into the margin and push the S-number into the sentence. On #/case/case_009, "S18" runs into "Progressively severe…" and "Other route, not met" hangs outside the rail. On #/check/case_009, "Met once charted" sits beside S16 out of column. This is clipped, overlapping text on a hero screen, so design and antiSlop are capped at 7.5. (2) The headline promise is only half visible: "missing evidence becomes a documentation request to the physician." No case in the demo reaches that verdict. The How page says so outright ("No denial in this demo set needs only a note, so the worklist shows no 'Ask the physician' filter"). On the one held denial (Emerson, case_009 › Next step), the note is a "Copy note to physician" button that copies text the biller never sees. (3) Status and labels contradict each other across screens. "✓ Counted in code: 38 days of conservative care (policy: 42)" shows a check glyph on a fact that fails. The same rule reads "Route not used" on the check and "Other route, not met" on the denial. Peyton Fictive (case_023) is labelled "Don't appeal yet" while the subline says the denial "can't be won on the chart". "Don't appeal yet" is painted red (`tone: "neg"`), but "Not winnable" is quiet grey, which inverts severity. The same Aetna snapshot (sha256 e12e0d12) is labelled "Policy on 08/03/2026" but shows "fetched 10/23/2026" on the case and "fetched 10/25/2026" on the check.

What does work, and is verifiable live:
- **Citation gate:** I edited "1 month" to "2 months" in Edit text. Export locked at once with "Blocked: 1 quote VOID", the bad quote struck through, and "closest L34220 · S47".
- **Model calls and cost:** a per-call table with tokens, seconds and dollars per step, with a correct total ($0.0596 across 34 calls).
- **Split vote:** the vote split and the Ultra referee are shown on the rule.
- **Computed figures:** "Counted in code" durations.
- **Versioning:** the CMS version on the date of service and the Aetna hash, with a copy button.
- **Policy watch:** the popover lists 9 citations.
- **Prevention:** the prior-auth check links to the later denial.
- **Live run:** a wrong passcode gets an inline error with a recovery hint.
- **Invariants:** the synthetic banner, the AMA line, "A person reviews and sends" and no send control all hold.

All gates are green: lint 0/0, inspect 0 FAIL / 0 WARN on 3 routes, detect [], node --check OK.

What holds the scores below 8:
- **Phone:** the case page is about 11,000px at 390px wide, with the full policy text inline and no one-region-at-a-time switch.
- **Self-narrating copy:** lines such as "demo dates and real dates are labelled", the S/n legend line and the How page's step-6 apology.
- **"VOID" stamp:** it is costume-like jargon.
- **Contradictory triage checklist:** a Fix & resubmit checklist says "Appeal only with that proof attached" right under "No clinical appeal is needed". That text comes from src/triage.py, so changing it needs the user's approval.
- **Duplicate quote in the drafted appeal:** the physical-therapy sentence is quoted twice in Clinical evidence. That is model output in demo/runs, so changing it needs the user's approval.

findings.title: Policy-margin status words overflow the 112px gutter and overprint sentence ids
findings.screen: #/check/case_009 (S16) and #/case/case_009 (S18), desktop 1440
findings.evidence: On check_009, '◐ Met once charted' starts left of the reading column and collides with 'S16' and the bullet. On case_009, 'Other route, not met' overprints 'S18' so it reads 'S1§Progressively…'. The cause is app.css:404 p.sent grid-template-columns: var(--gutter-sentence) with --gutter-sentence:112px (app.css:75) and .gut .w {white-space:nowrap} (app.css:409).
findings.fix: Let gutter words wrap: .gut .w {white-space:normal; text-align:right; max-width:calc(var(--gutter-sentence) - 16px); text-wrap:balance}. Alternatively raise --gutter-sentence to 136px and update .hdg/.fold/.sheet-head margins, which already use the variable. Shorten the gutter vocabulary in app.js too ('Once charted', 'Other route'). Verify that no gutter label crosses into the sentence column on case_009, case_015 and check_009.

findings.title: 'Counted in code' shows a checkmark on an unmet waiting period
findings.screen: #/case/case_009 and #/check/case_009, rule card Policy S16
findings.evidence: The Blocks rule S16 shows '✓ Counted in code: 38 days of conservative care (policy: 42)'. countedHtml() (app.js:151-152) always renders g("check"), whether or not k.n >= k.t.days, so a green-style check sits next to a count that misses the threshold.
findings.fix: In countedHtml, choose the glyph and word from the comparison: if k.n >= k.t.days use g('check') and append ' · meets the wait'; otherwise use g('x') (negative ink) and append ' · short by ' + (k.t.days - k.n) + ' days'. Status then always pairs a glyph with a word and agrees with the coverage path ('Not met: 38 of 42 days charted').
